title: DeepMind reinforcement-learning controller shapes TCV plasmas, including sustained twin 'droplets'
summary: A deep RL controller commanding all 19 TCV coils produced and held elongated, negative-triangularity, snowflake and twin-droplet plasmas at EPFL's Swiss Plasma Center (Nature, 16 February 2022).
account: Degrave et al. (Nature, published 16 February 2022; received 14 July 2021) describe an architecture in which a single deep neural network learns in simulation to command the full set of 19 magnetic control coils of the Tokamak à Configuration Variable (TCV), a research tokamak at the Swiss Plasma Center, EPFL. Deployed on the real device, the controller produced and controlled elongated conventional shapes and advanced configurations such as negative triangularity and 'snowflake' plasmas, tracking location, current and shape; in one demonstration it established a snowflake with X-points 34 cm apart and narrowed the separation to 6.6 cm with a combined RMSE of 3.7 cm. It also sustained 'droplets', two separate plasmas maintained simultaneously in the vessel. MIT Technology Review (16 February 2022) reported that the AI controlled the real reactor without additional fine-tuning and quoted independent expert Jonathan Citrin of the Dutch Institute for Fundamental Energy Research and Swiss Plasma Center director Ambrogio Fasoli. The experiment dates are not given; the date used is the paper's publication date.
purpose: The controller was built to shape and maintain plasmas in TCV from high-level objectives; the configurations produced, including droplets, were its intended use.
system: DeepMind deep reinforcement learning magnetic controller for TCV (MLP policy commanding 19 coils)
developer: DeepMind, with the Swiss Plasma Center, EPFL
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the result is a control capability on a research tokamak rather than an accuracy gain over a baseline.

ratings.reason: The Swiss Plasma Center gained a controller that the paper calls a notable advance for tokamak feedback control, with reduced design effort for new configurations and new droplet experiments.
No societal outcome beyond research progress is documented.

ai_role.statement: The RL policy directly issued the coil voltage commands during the discharges, so the configurations are the controller's output; the evidence is the peer-reviewed paper co-authored by the maker (DeepMind) and the operator (EPFL) plus an independent news report quoting an outside expert. Developer and deployer collaborated on the paper.

Access to machine time on a research tokamak
